G1513.abbott_html: conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect questions. I. Conditional, if; 1. c. indic. expressing a general assumption; (a) pres. seq. indic, pres. al. seq. imperat. al. seq. fut. indic. al. seq. pf. or aor. with negation in apodosis, al. similarly, seq. impf. seq. quæst. (b) fut. (c) pf. al. (d) aor. al. 2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: al. 3. Of an unfulfilled condition, c. indic, impf. aor. or plpf. seq. ἄν, c. imp. or aor. 4. C. indic. after verbs denoting wonder, etc. sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: al. 5. C. indic. as in LXX (, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): (LXX) (LXX). 6. Rarely (cl.) c. optat. to express a merely possible condition: I Pe3:14, 17. II. Interrogative, if, whether. 1. As in cl. in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc. c. indic. pres. al. fut. al. aor. al. c. subjc. aor. 2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, al. v. WM, 639 f. Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: (Tr. WH, txt.), al. III. With other particles. 1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, v.s. ἄρα, γε. 2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also; but even if. 3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: al. 4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: al. 5. καὶ εἰ, even if, v.s. καί 6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: (only); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic. 7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν, in oaths, surely (, al.). 8. εἴ πως, if haply. 9. εἴτε. εἴτε, whether. or: al.

(b) of approach, to or towards: al. (c) before pl. and collective nouns, among: al. (d) Of a limit reached, unto, on, upon: al. c. acc. pers. (as in Ep. and Ion.) (e) elliptical: ἐπιστολαὶ εἰς Δαμασκόν; ἡ διακονία μου ἡ εἰς Ἱ. metaph. of entrance into a certain state or condition, or of approach or direction towards some end, εἰς τ. ὄνομα, M, Pr., 200. 2. Of direction; (a) after verbs of seeing: al. metaph. of the mind, al. (b) after verbs of speaking: al. 3. After verbs of rest; (a) in "pregnant" construction, implying previous motion (cl. v. WM, 516; Bl. §39, 3; M, Pr., 234f.): al. (b) by an assimilation general in late Gk = ἐν: (but v. Westc, in l.), al. II. Of time, for, unto; 1. accentuating the duration expressed by the acc. εἰς τ. αἰῶνα; εἰς γενεὰς καὶ γ. εἰς τ. διηνεκές, al. 2. Of a point or limit of time, unto, up to, until; of entrance into a future period, εις τὸ μέλλον, next (year), (but c. ICC, in l.); εἰς τ. μεταξὺ σάββατον, on the next Sabbath; εἰς τὸ πάλιν (v.s. πάλιν. III. Of result, after verbs of changing, joining, dividing, etc. στρέφειν εἰς; μετας-; μεταλλάσσειν; σχίζειν εἰς δύο, al. predicatively with εἴναι. IV. Of relation, to, towards, for, in regard to (so in cl. but more freq. in late Gk. εἰς encroaching on the simple dat. which it has wholly displaced in MGr. Jannaris, Gr., §1541; Robertson, Gr., 594; Deiss. BS, 117f.): al. ἀγάπη εἰς, al. χρηστός; φρονεῖν εἰς; θαρρεῖν. V. Of the end or object: εὔθετος εἰς; σόφος; ἰσχύειν; εἰς τοῦτο, al. ἀφορίζειν εἰς; indicating purpose, εἰς φόβον; εἰς ἔνδειξιν; εἰς τό, c. inf. (= ἵνα or ὥστε; Bl. §71, 5; M, Pr., 218ff.): al. VI. G1537.abbott_html: prep. c. gen. from out of, from (see Addendum, p. 492).This entry is included here, but in the print version the entry is found on p. 492. prep. c. gen. of motion outwards, separation from (opp. to εἰς; = Lat. e, ex), from out of, from among, from. I. Of Place, 1. of motion, out of, forth from, off from: al. esp. after verbs of motion, al. constr. praeg. σώζειν (διας.) ἐκ. Metaph. ἐκ τ. χειρός (-ῶν), seq. gen. pers. πίνειν (q.v.) ἐκ; of the place from which an action proceeds. 2. Of change from one place or condition to another: al. c. ellips. of verb of motion, al. 3. Of separation or distinction from a number, before collective or pl. nouns: al. after εἷς, al. οὐδείς, al. πολλοί, al. τις, al. τίς, al. in partitive phrase as subject of sentence; Hebraistically, ἐκ μέσου seq. gen. = ἐκ (Heb. מִתֹּוךְ), al. 4. Of position or direction (so in cl. = ἔξω): ἐκ δεξιῶν; ἐξ ἐναντίας, (metaph. ); ἐκ ῥιζῶν (i.e. utterly). II. Of Time, 1. of the point of time from which, from, since: ἐκ γενετῆς, cf. al. 2. Of succession in time: ἐκ δευτέρου, a second time, al. cf. ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας, from day to day. III. Of Origin, 1. of nativity, lineage, race: κοίτην (ἐν γαστρί) ἔχειν; γεννᾶν ἐκ, ff. γεννᾶσθαι (γίνεσθαι) ἐκ; ἐκ πνεύματος (θεοῦ), ff. al. ἔρχεσθαι, εἶναι, etc. ἐκ τ. πολέως; φυλῆς, al. τ. ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου; ὁ ὢν ἐκ τ. γῆς. 2. Of the author, occasion or source: al. ἐκ (τ.) θεοῦ; ἐκ τ. πατρός, al. ἐκ τ. γῆς ἐστιν, λαλεῖ; εκ καρδίας, cf. ἐκ ψυχῆς; ἐκ πίστεως; κρίνειν ἐκ. 3. Of the agent, after passive verbs: al. freq. in Re after αδικεῖσθαι, etc. 4. Of cause, dependence, source of supply: τ. πόνου (των); τ. φωνῶν; ἐκ τούτου, (but v. Meyer, in ll.); ἐκ θεοῦ λαλεῖν; ἐκ τ. ἀληθείας εἶναι; ὁ ἐκ πίστεως; οἱ (ὄντες) ἐκ περιτομῆς; πίνειν ἐκ, al. θερίζειν; μετέχειν ἐκ (= partit. gen.); c. inf. ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν. 5. Of material: al. allied to which is its use of price (= cl. gen.): cf. IV. By attraction = ἐν (cl.): τὰ ἐκ τ. οἰκιας; τ. ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν; ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ. V. Adverbial phrases: ἐξ ἀνάγκης; ἐξ ἰσότητος; ἐκ μέρους; ἐκ μέτρου; ἐκ συμφώνου, I Co 7:5. VI. in composition, ἐκ signifies, 1. procession, removal: ἐκβαίνω, ἐκβάλλω. 2. Opening out, unfolding: ἐκτείνω; metaph. ἐξαγγάλλω. 3. Origin: ἔκγονος. 4. Completeness: ἐξαπορέω, ἐκπληρόω, ἐκτελέω.
